issues.description: Function signature mismatch for simulate_ghz_state: the template defines simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits: int) -> dict[str, int] (no shots parameter) but the problem statement and solution expect simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits, shots). The template's docstring and asserts reference a shots parameter (e.g., assert shots > 0) while the function signature omits it, causing an API mismatch that will prevent students from implementing and running the GHZ simulation or matching tests that call the two-argument form.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template function signature to include the shots parameter and use it consistently. For example: def simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits: int, shots: int) -> dict[str, int]: Then add the missing assert for shots (assert shots > 0) and ensure the function body passes shots to measure_all or otherwise uses shots when sampling. This aligns the template API with the problem statement and solution while preserving the pedagogical intent.

issues.description: Function signature mismatch for the GHZ simulation routine: the problem statement describes and the solution implements simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits, shots) (i.e., it expects two parameters: num_qubits and shots). The template defines simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits) (only one parameter). The template's docstring and body even refer to 'shots' and contain an assert for shots > 0, but the function declaration does not provide that parameter. This inconsistency will confuse students: the requirement (and tests) expect a two-argument function (num_qubits, shots), while the template presents a one-argument stub, causing a mismatch when mapping the specification to the starter code and preventing straightforward implementation and testing.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template function signature to accept the shots parameter to match the problem statement and solution: def simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits: int, shots: int) -> dict[str, int]:. Update the function body and asserts accordingly (assert shots > 0) and implement measurement sampling consistent with the docstring (or leave clear TODOs referencing the expected two-argument behavior) so students can directly map the requirement to the stub.
